headline: OpenAI staffers fund rival super PAC to counter pro-industry lobbying by their own president
summary: Seven current and one former OpenAI employee have donated over $215,000 to Guardrails Alliance, a super PAC advocating for stricter AI regulations, directly opposing a pro-industry PAC backed by OpenAI's president.
details: A group of current and former OpenAI employees has donated over $215,000 to Guardrails Alliance, a super PAC advocating for stricter AI regulations. This group aims to be a counterweight to Leading the Future, a pro-AI industry super PAC backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman.

Seven current and one former OpenAI employee have contributed to Guardrails Alliance, as revealed to WIRED ahead of the super PAC's first quarterly FEC filing. Two employees will appear in the initial filing, with five more in future disclosures.

Juan Felipe Cerón Uribe, a research engineer at OpenAI since 2022, made one of the largest donations from an employee, contributing $200,000. Cerón Uribe stated he is concerned his research on mitigating AI's societal harms will be wasted without strong guardrails.

He explicitly cited tech billionaires like Greg Brockman funding Leading the Future to keep AI unregulated as his motivation. Cerón Uribe expressed satisfaction that Guardrails Alliance is pushing back against this agenda.

These donations highlight growing internal tensions within OpenAI regarding its stance on AI policy. Brockman's $50 million commitment to Leading the Future has previously sparked concern among some employees.

OpenAI leaders have attempted to distance the company from Leading the Future, stating Brockman's involvement is personal. However, some employees are now using their personal funds to directly oppose the pro-industry lobbying efforts.

Shaunna Thomas, cofounder of Guardrails Alliance, aims to raise $15 million this election cycle, despite the financial disparity. She believes exposing the actions of pro-AI PACs will leverage existing public opinion against them.

Leading the Future, launched with Brockman as a key supporter, aims to "oppose policies that stifle innovation." The PAC has previously attempted to hinder campaigns of politicians advocating for AI safety laws.

headline_marked: [[PS5 emulation explodes]], booting commercial games like GTA V and Astro Bot
headline: PS5 emulation explodes, booting commercial games like GTA V and Astro Bot
summary: Driven by Sony's end of physical disc production and GTA VI anticipation, emulators like SharpEmu and KytyPS5 are now booting recent PS5 titles, including full gameplay for some.
details: The PS5 emulation scene, long dormant, has suddenly exploded with new projects. This surge is driven by Sony's decision to halt physical disc production and the upcoming release of GTA VI, creating unprecedented demand. Emulators are now rapidly hitting milestones, booting recent PS5 titles.

SharpEmu, a Windows-based PS5 emulator written in C#, acts as a translation layer. It allows PCs to execute CPU instructions natively while translating OS-specific API calls and graphics. While 2D titles like Dreaming Sarah run smoothly, 3D titles are harder.

Initially, Demon's Souls remake only booted to the startup screen on SharpEmu. However, a major breakthrough saw Discord user RShantila successfully boot Astro Bot, a 2024 PlayStation exclusive. This progress is remarkably fast, outpacing PS4 emulation at a similar stage.

Another significant project is KytyPS5, revived by developer Nmzik after being abandoned in 2022. Within weeks, the new fork focusing solely on PS5 can boot commercial games running on Unreal Engine 4/5, Unity, and other custom engines.

KytyPS5 successfully booted Silent Hill: The Short Message to its menu screen. More impressively, recent updates show PowerWash Simulator and Pac-Man World running with properly rendered graphics and functional gameplay. Performance and stability details are yet unknown.

KytyPS5 version 0.0.3 also managed to boot the commercial PS5 version of Grand Theft Auto V. It reached the loading screens, main splash art, and allowed navigation of in-game display settings. Further updates have improved its shader compiler, memory management, and audio support.

While SharpEmu and KytyPS5 lead the charge, RPCSX is another notable research project dedicated to understanding PS4 and PS5 software. The team, experienced from RPCS3, is working towards booting games from the user interface.

The rapid development in PS5 emulation is astonishing, with projects achieving significant progress in a short timeframe. At this trajectory, fully playable GTA V on these emulators could be a reality as early as next month, showcasing the community's swift advancements.
